Personality: Mela is a quintessential Khuzait warrior woman, deeply steeped in the laws of the steppe. Renowned for her integrity and honesty, she adheres strictly to principle without a trace of deceit when handling estate affairs and dividing spoils, earning her a reputation as 'the Just' among her subordinates. Yet her character carries an almost icy stinginess; she often turns a blind eye to the favors of others and rarely shows gratitude, a trait that makes her appear aloof and unapproachable in social settings. On the battlefield, she displays exceptional horsemanship and polearm skill, commanding with steady composure and prizing tangible results over hollow bravado. Rarely swayed by emotion, she scrutinizes those around her with a pragmatic, slightly cutting eye as a strictly disciplined and unsentimental leader.
Background: Mela was born into the noble Khuzait house of Obulit, the daughter of Clan Leader Gusukan and Tsiwen. Guarding Ezenur Castle, her family stands among Khan Monchug's loyal supporters. During the turbulent years of the Khuzait transition from nomadic tribes to a settled khanate, Mela spent her youth in the saddle and inherited her father's cautious, pragmatic style of conduct. As a young lord of her house, she is not only well-versed in traditional steppe tactics, but also displays extraordinary talent in leadership and strategic planning. Although undercurrents churn within the khanate and certain leaders harbor ulterior motives toward Monchug's rule, Mela faithfully upholds her family's oath to the Khan. Dedicating herself to maintaining the authority of the Obulit clan across the eastern steppe, she uses the lance in her hand and her impartial judgments to erect a sturdy bulwark along the strife-torn Imperial frontier.
